### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.ai

### Question

For example, I select the `"first range"` by `vin"`, but I want to jump to `"second range"` instead.
The current solution is escaping to normal mode and type `vin"` again, which is not too convenient.
Is it possible to have a keymap to jump to next selection of previous triggered textobject type directly, in visual mode?

```
This is "first range" to be selected
...
...
Now I want to select this "second range" in visual mode directly
without repeating `vin"`
```

Question
For example, I select the "first range" by vin", but I want to jump to "second range" instead.
The current solution is escaping to normal mode and type vin" again, which is not too convenient.
Is it possible to have a keymap to jump to next selection of previous triggered textobject type directly, in visual mode?

comment_data.body:
'mini.ai' selection supports what is called in the docs [consecutive application](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/ccfc8c35cac348070a9528410c794459c4cc2eeb/doc/mini-ai.txt#L17). Meaning visual selection can be updated without leaving Visual mode. This is true for any variant of textobject: without "modifiers", "next", "last".

So for the example in this question:
- Typing `vinq` (when cursor is on the first column of the first line) will visually select `first range`.
- Typing `inq` (*without `v`*) will select `second range`. The same effect could have been achieved with `in"`.
- Moreover, with selection from the previous step still active, typing `ilq` will again select `first range`. And so on.
